title: 1940s touring acts: Erskine Hawkins, Wynonie Harris, Andy Kirk with Big June Richmond
summary: Stephens recalls 1949 shows by Erskine Hawkins, Mabel Scott, Gatemouth Brown and blues concerts at the Dewdrop and Foster's, then Andy Kirk's 1942 visit; the tape is paused.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: We left off. Yeah, well let's fill in where we left off. Let's go back to the 40s and we'll update things. Some of the things we didn't cover, like when Oyskin Hawkins came here in 1949. He played at the Booker T. Washington Auditorium. And incidentally, Mabel Scott played at Foster's Rainbow Room, and Gate Mouth Brown played together. And then they went over to the Dewdrop, and they did a midnight show like that was back there in 1949. And I think I discussed with you earlier about Amos Milburn and Winoni Harris and Jewel King and all those people. And then Roy Brown and Winoni Harris, they played a series of blues concerts that went from Dewdrop to Foster's. And I think the last time I saw Amos Milburn, he was playing at the Robin Hood. That's a club that's toned down. It was on the corner of Jackson and Simone Bolivia, Simon Bolivia, as some people say in that particular neighborhood. And then of course, like we didn't cover, in 1942, when Andy Kirk came here. He came with Big June Richmond, who weighed about 300 pounds at the time, because she's living in Europe right now. And she was a tremendous vocalist. And one of the most favorite singers. One of the most famous people. One of the most famous people.
